claim: Adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP) is responsible for the transport of very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) and corresponding CoA-esters across the peroxisomal membrane.
source: Adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP) is responsible for the transport of very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) and corresponding CoA-esters across the peroxisomal membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known function of ALDP, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Dysfunction of ALDP leads to peroxisomal metabolic disorder exemplified by X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD).
source: Dysfunction of ALDP leads to peroxisomal metabolic disorder exemplified by X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and represents established knowledge about the disease.

claim: Hundreds of ALD-causing mutations have been identified on ALDP.
source: Hundreds of ALD-causing mutations have been identified on ALDP.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to mutation databases in the introduction.

claim: The cryo-electron microscopy structure of human ALDP has a nominal resolution of 3.4 Å.
source: Here we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human ALDP with nominal resolution at 3.4 Å.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental cryo-EM data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ALDP exhibits a cytosolic-facing conformation.
source: ALDP exhibits a cytosolic-facing conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ALDP has two substrate binding cavities formed by the transmembrane domains.
source: Compared to other lipid ATP-binding cassette transporters, ALDP has two substrate binding cavities formed by the transmembrane domains.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The structural organization of ALDP may be suitable for the coordination of VLCFAs.
source: Such structural organization may be suitable for the coordination of VLCFAs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observed structural features.

claim: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an inherited disease characterized by progressive demyelination of the central nervous system.
source: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an inherited disease characterized by progressive demyelination of the central nervous system (Berger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation support.

claim: Loss of myelin slows down the transmission of nerve impulses and triggers neuroinflammation.
source: Loss of myelin slows down the transmission of nerve impulses and triggers neuroinflammation (Ferrer et al., 2010; Kettwig et al., 2021; Singh et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from multiple references.

claim: Pathogenesis of ALD is tightly associated with mutations on the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP).
source: Pathogenesis of ALD is tightly associated with mutations on the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP), which transports very-long-chain fatty acid-CoAs (VLCFA-CoAs) from cytosol into the peroxisome (Figure 1; Mosser et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and reference to Figure 1.

claim: ALDP transports very-long-chain fatty acid-CoAs (VLCFA-CoAs) from cytosol into the peroxisome.
source: Pathogenesis of ALD is tightly associated with mutations on the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP), which transports very-long-chain fatty acid-CoAs (VLCFA-CoAs) from cytosol into the peroxisome (Figure 1; Mosser et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Over 900 disease-derived mutations have been identified on ALDP.
source: Over 900 disease-derived mutations have been identified on ALDP (https://adrenoleukodystrophy.info/mutations-biochemistry/mutations-biochemistry).
evidence: This is stated with reference to a mutation database.

claim: ALDP is also known as ABCD1.
source: ALDP, also known as ABCD1, belongs to the ATP-binding cassette sub-family D.
evidence: This is stated as an established nomenclature fact.

claim: ALDP belongs to the ATP-binding cassette sub-family D.
source: ALDP, also known as ABCD1, belongs to the ATP-binding cassette sub-family D.
evidence: This is stated as an established classification.

claim: The ATP-binding cassette sub-family D has four members: ABCD1, ABCD2, ABCD3, and ABCD4.
source: The other three members are ALDP-related protein (ALDRP/ABCD2; Lombard-Platet et al., 1996), PMP70/ABCD3 (Kamijo et al., 1990), and a cobalamin transporter ABCD4 (Coelho et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations for each member.

claim: ABCD1–3 are distributed on peroxisomes.
source: ABCD1–3 are distributed on peroxisomes, while ABCD4 is localized on lysosomes (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: ABCD4 is localized on lysosomes.
source: ABCD1–3 are distributed on peroxisomes, while ABCD4 is localized on lysosomes (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: ALDP and ALDRP transport VLCFA with different specificities.
source: ALDP and ALDRP transport VLCFA with different specificities (van Roermund et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: ALDRP may compensate for the function loss of ALDP.
source: ALDRP may compensate for the function loss of ALDP (Holzinger et al., 1997; Liu et al., 1999; Lombard-Platet et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: PMP70 was reported to transport LCFA-CoA.
source: PMP70 was reported to transport LCFA-CoA (Ranea-Robles et al., 2021; van Roermund et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: In the presence of C22:0-CoA, ALDP exhibits robust ATP hydrolysis with the Vmax of ~193 ± 8.2 mol Pi min−1 mol−1 protein.
source: In the presence of C22:0-CoA, ALDP exhibits robust ATP hydrolysis with the Vmax of ~193 ± 8.2 mol Pi min−1 mol−1 protein and Km value of ~0.17 µM C22:0-CoA (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: In the presence of C22:0-CoA, ALDP exhibits a Km value of ~0.17 µM C22:0-CoA.
source: In the presence of C22:0-CoA, ALDP exhibits robust ATP hydrolysis with the Vmax of ~193 ± 8.2 mol Pi min−1 mol−1 protein and Km value of ~0.17 µM C22:0-CoA (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated with reference to experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: The structure of human ALDP reveals an assembly of two identical subunits that exhibit a domain-swapped arrangement.
source: The structure of human ALDP reveals an assembly of two identical subunits that exhibit a domain-swapped arrangement (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2 and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated with reference to structural data in figures.

claim: Each subunit of ALDP contains six transmembrane helices.
source: Each subunit contains six transmembrane helices (TMs; Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with reference to structural data in figures.

claim: A short helix located at the peroxisomal side (extracellular helix [EH]) is a featured structural element of ALDP based on sequence alignment.
source: A short helix located at the peroxisomal side (extracellular helix [EH]) is a featured structural element of ALDP based on sequence alignment (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with reference to sequence alignment data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Two coiled-coil domain-like densities at the C-terminus were observed in ALDP.
source: Two coiled-coil domain-like densities at the C-terminus were observed (C-terminal helix [CH]).
evidence: This is stated based on structural observation.

claim: The local resolution of the C-terminal helix densities is estimated to be ~4.0 Å.
source: The local resolution of these densities is estimated to be ~4.0 Å, which is not accurate to build an atomic model.
evidence: This is stated based on resolution analysis of the cryo-EM data.

claim: Four other groups independently reported ALDP structures in different states during submission of this study.
source: During submission of this study, four other groups independently reported ALDP structures in different states (Chen et al., 2022; Le et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022; Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to concurrent publications.

claim: The structure reported in this study is the ligand-free state as no substrates were supplemented during purification.
source: Our structure is the ligand-free state as no substrates were supplemented during purification.
evidence: This is stated based on the experimental protocol used.

claim: Two unknown densities were observed at the crevice of TMDs in the ligand-free structure.
source: We observed two unknown densities at the crevice of TMDs, which were also reported in the ligand-free structure by Chen et al., 2022.
evidence: This is stated based on structural observation and corroborated by another study.

claim: When superimposed to the oleoyl-CoA- or C22:0-CoA-bound structures, the unknown densities partially overlap with the substrates.
source: When superimposed to the oleoyl-CoA- or C22:0-CoA-bound structures, the unknown densities partially overlap with the substrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The observation of unknown densities indicates a probable extrusion of the unknown densities during substrate loading.
source: Such observation indicates a probable extrusion of the unknown densities during substrate loading.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural observation.

claim: The distance between TM4 and TM6 at the juxta-membrane region changes from 23.6 Å to 13.1 Å upon substrate binding.
source: For instance, the distance between TM4 and TM6 at the juxta-membrane region changes from 23.6 Å to 13.1 Å upon substrate binding and further gets closed to 5.7 Å in the presence of ATP.
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison measurements.

claim: The distance between TM4 and TM6 at the juxta-membrane region further gets closed to 5.7 Å in the presence of ATP.
source: For instance, the distance between TM4 and TM6 at the juxta-membrane region changes from 23.6 Å to 13.1 Å upon substrate binding and further gets closed to 5.7 Å in the presence of ATP.
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison measurements.

claim: The nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) undergo continuously spatial rearrangement during the transport cycle.
source: The nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) undergo continuously spatial rearrangement.
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison across different states.

claim: The TM4-6 and TM1-2 bend to open the peroxisomal side exit for substrate.
source: Consequently, the TM4-6 and TM1-2 bend to open the peroxisomal side exit for substrate (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: Conformational change of TMDs is accompanied with the movement of NBDs and the disappearance of EH or CH.
source: Conformational change of TMDs is accompanied with the movement of NBDs and the disappearance of EH or CH.
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison across different states.

claim: 970 ALD-associated mutations in ALDP affecting 232 residues have been reported.
source: 970 ALD-associated mutations in ALDP affecting 232 residues have been reported.
evidence: This is stated based on compilation of reported mutations.

claim: Among the 232 residues with ALD-associated mutations, 88 harbor mutations to two or more types of amino acids.
source: Among these 232 residues, 88 harbor mutations to two or more types of amino acids, which we defined as hotspot residues.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of mutation data.

claim: The 88 hotspot residues can be roughly classified into 3 groups based on structural mapping.
source: Based on the structural mapping, the 88 hotspot residues can be roughly classified into 3 groups (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated based on structural analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The first group of 10 residues lines along the substrate-binding cavity.
source: The first group of 10 residues lines along the substrate-binding cavity.
evidence: This is stated based on structural mapping.

claim: The first group of residues likely play a role in substrate coordination and delivery.
source: These residues likely play a role in substrate coordination and delivery.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of these residues.

claim: The second group of 35 residues is located in other region of the TMDs, which undergoes conformational changes.
source: The second group of 35 residues is located in other region of the TMDs, which undergoes conformational changes.
evidence: This is stated based on structural mapping and analysis.

claim: The third group of 43 residues is located on the NBDs that may have influence on ATP hydrolysis.
source: The third group of 43 residues is located on the NBDs that may have influence on ATP hydrolysis (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated based on structural mapping with speculative functional interpretation.

claim: All six disease-derived mutants (W339R, S342P, G343V, A396T, Q544R, and T693M) exhibit decreased transport toward three species of VLCFA-CoA.
source: All six disease-derived mutants exhibit decreased transport toward three species of VLCFA-CoA.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental transport assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Five mutants (W339R, G343V, A396T, Q544R, and T693M) show abrogated ATP hydrolysis except for the mutation S342P.
source: Five mutants show abrogated ATP hydrolysis except for the mutation S342P.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental ATPase assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: All the selected mutants show puncta distribution and colocalize with catalase, suggesting their normal trafficking to the peroxisomes.
source: Compared with A95D, a disease-causing mutation known to not colocalize with peroxisome and reduce the C24:0 β-oxidation (Morita et al., 2013), all the selected mutants show puncta distribution and colocalize with catalase, suggesting their normal trafficking to the peroxisomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The similar Tm values of purified mutant proteins rule out the instability-caused functional abrogation.
source: The similar Tm values of purified mutant proteins rule out the instability-caused functional abrogation (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated based on thermal stability assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the AF-model, T693 is located near W664, which is surrounded by ALD mutants on the NBD.
source: In the AF-model, T693 is located near W664, which is surrounded by ALD mutants on the NBD.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of the AlphaFold predicted model.

claim: The distance between the side chains of T693 and W664 can reach in 3.4 Å.
source: The distance between the side chains of T693 and W664 can reach in 3.4 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated based on measurement in the AlphaFold model shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Replacement of Thr by Met residue with large side chain may affect the neighboring residues near W664 to disturb the ATP hydrolysis.
source: Replacement of Thr by Met residue with large side chain may affect the neighboring residues near W664 to disturb the ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on structural analysis.

claim: Alanine substitution of S164/Y310 and E291/R518 has negligible influence on the ATP hydrolysis.
source: For the four designed constructs, alanine substitution of S164/Y310 and E291/R518 has negligible influence on the ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental ATPase assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Alanine substitution of S164/Y310 and E291/R518 decreases lipid transport because destabilization of the interaction between these residues may disturb the conformational changes during substrate translocation.
source: By contrast, the lipid transport decreased because destabilization of the interaction between these residues may disturb the conformational changes during substrate translocation.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental transport data with speculative mechanistic interpretation.

claim: Deletion of the EH (Δ364–374) may generate structural constraints between TM5 and TM6 during the conformational change of ALDP.
source: As one featured structural element, deletion of the EH (Δ364–374) may generate structural constraints between TM5 and TM6 during the conformational change of ALDP (Chen et al., 2022; Le et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated with citation support and represents a speculative interpretation.

claim: Truncation of CH (Δ683–745) does not change the assembly of NBD but affects the conformational changes between the two protomers.
source: Truncation of CH (Δ683–745) does not change the assembly of NBD but affects the conformational changes between the two protomers, thus the ATP hydrolysis level slightly decreased with abrogated lipid transport.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ALDP harbors two substrate-binding pockets that expand perpendicularly to the membrane.
source: Typically, ALDP harbors two substrate-binding pockets that expand perpendicularly to the membrane, but ABCB4 binds one phosphatidylcholine (PC) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: ABCB4 binds one phosphatidylcholine (PC).
source: Typically, ALDP harbors two substrate-binding pockets that expand perpendicularly to the membrane, but ABCB4 binds one phosphatidylcholine (PC) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated based on structural comparison with citation support.

claim: The dimension of one binding pocket is ~1695 Å3 for C22:0-CoA.
source: The dimension of one binding pocket is ~1695 Å3 for C22:0-CoA and ~1236 Å3 for PC calculated by ProteinPlus (Schöning-Stierand et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated based on computational calculation using ProteinPlus.

claim: The dimension of one binding pocket is ~1236 Å3 for PC.
source: The dimension of one binding pocket is ~1695 Å3 for C22:0-CoA and ~1236 Å3 for PC calculated by ProteinPlus (Schöning-Stierand et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated based on computational calculation using ProteinPlus.

claim: The length of C22:0-CoA (~55 Å) is larger than PC (~40 Å).
source: Regardless of the flexibility, the length of C22:0-CoA (~55 Å) is larger than PC (~40 Å) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is stated based on structural measurement shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5B.

claim: The PC molecule has two acyl tails that can be coordinated by ABCB4.
source: The PC molecule has two acyl tails that can be coordinated by ABCB4.
evidence: This is stated based on structural knowledge of PC and ABCB4.

claim: The VLCFAs have only one hydrophobic tail.
source: The VLCFAs have only one hydrophobic tail.
evidence: This is stated based on chemical knowledge of VLCFA structure.

claim: More residues in a larger binding pocket of ALDP may help in stabilizing the flexible long tail of VLCFA-CoA.
source: More residues in a larger binding pocket of ALDP may help in stabilizing the flexible long tail of VLCFA-CoA.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on structural comparison.

claim: The EH and CH facilitate conformational changes to expand the binding pocket.
source: The EH and CH facilitate conformational changes to expand the binding pocket.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis and mutational data.

claim: The recombinant ALDP was expressed using the Bac-to-bac system.
source: The recombinant ALDP was expressed using the Bac-to-bac system (Invitrogen).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the experimental protocol.

claim: ALDP was overexpressed in Sf9 insect cells grown in the serum-free medium.
source: ALDP was overexpressed in Sf9 insect cells grown in the serum-free medium (Gibco).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the experimental protocol.

claim: The cryo-EM samples were imaged on an FEI 300 kV Titan Krios transmission electron microscope.
source: The sample was imaged on an FEI 300 kV Titan Krios transmission electron microscope equipped with a Cs corrector and Gatan GIF Quantum energy filter (slit width 20 eV), recorded by a Gatan K2 Summit detector with a nominal magnification of ×640,000.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the experimental protocol.

claim: A series of defocus values from –1.5 to –1.8 µm was used during data collection.
source: A series of defocus values from –1.5 to –1.8 µm was used during data collection.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the experimental protocol.

claim: In total, 1,259,972 particles were auto-picked from 1922 movie stacks.
source: In total, 1,259,972 particles were auto-picked from these 1922 movie stacks using Gautomatch (developed by Kai Zhang, http://www.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/kzhang/Gautomatch) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: After two-dimensional classification, 472,168 particles were selected to generate the initial model.
source: After two-dimensional classification, 472,168 particles were selected to generate the initial model with a mask diameter of 200 Å in C1 symmetry.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the data processing workflow.

claim: A total of 289,321 particles were selected from the local angular searching 3D classification after removing the redundant particles and particles from bad classes.
source: A total of 289,321 particles were selected from the local angular searching 3D classification after removing the redundant particles and particles from bad classes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: After multi-reference 3D classification, 135,662 particles were selected for autorefinement with C2 symmetry, resulting a map at 3.4 Å resolution.
source: After multi-reference 3D classification, 135,662 particles were selected for autorefinement with C2 symmetry, resulting a map at 3.4 Å resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the final refinement.

claim: The structure of ABCD4 was used as a template for the model building of ALDP.
source: The structure of ABCD4 was used as a template for the model building of ALDP.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the model building approach.

claim: Chromatographic separation was achieved using Q Exactive HF LC-MS/MS system and Phenomenex Luna 5 µm C5 column.
source: Chromatographic separation was achieved using Q Exactive HF LC-MS/MS system and Phenomenex Luna 5 µm C5 column (i.d. 100×2.0 mm).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the LC-MS/MS protocol.

claim: Both WT ALDP and mutant constructs were subcloned into a pCAG vector and expressed in HEK293F cells.
source: Both WT ALDP and mutant constructs were subcloned into a pCAG vector and expressed in HEK293F cells (Invitrogen).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the expression system for functional assays.

claim: Transfected cells were harvested after 60 hr for VLCFA-CoA measurement.
source: Transfected cells were harvested after 60 hr.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the experimental protocol.

claim: The malachite green ATPase assay was chosen to exhibit the ABCD1 ATPase activity in the presence of C22:0-CoA.
source: The malachite green ATPase assay was chosen to exhibit the ABCD1 ATPase activity in the presence of C22:0-CoA (behenoyl coenzyme A, ammonium salt) as previously described (Baykov et al., 1988).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section with citation support.

claim: wtABCD1 and mutants were deleted N-terminal 54 residues to improve stability for ATPase assay.
source: For determining ATP hydrolysis capacity, wtABCD1 and mutants were deleted N-terminal 54 residues to improve stability.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the protein preparation for ATPase assay.

claim: The thermal stability assay was performed by measuring intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence and light back-scattering using a Prometheus NT.48 device.
source: The thermal stability assay was performed by measuring intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence and light back-scattering for fragment screening by a Prometheus NT.48 device (NanoTemper Technologies GmbH, Munich, Germany) (Ahmad et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section with citation support.

claim: wtABCD1 and mutations were purified in LMNG/CHS and concentrated to 0.5 mg/ml for thermal stability assay.
source: wtABCD1 and mutations were purified in LMNG/CHS and concentrated to 0.5 mg/ml, after centrifuged at 14,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C, supernatant was loaded with standard capillaries (NanoTemper Technologies GmbH, Munich, Germany; Cat# PR-C002) into the Prometheus device and subjected to a linear thermal ramp (1°C/min, from 25 to 95°C) and collected fluorescence at 350 nm and 330 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the thermal stability assay protocol.

claim: A95D is a disease-causing mutation known to not colocalize with peroxisome and reduce the C24:0 β-oxidation.
source: Compared with A95D, a disease-causing mutation known to not colocalize with peroxisome and reduce the C24:0 β-oxidation (Morita et al., 2013), all the selected mutants show puncta distribution and colocalize with catalase, suggesting their normal trafficking to the peroxisomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: High structural similarities are found between ALDP and ABCD2 or ABCD3 and ABCD4.
source: High structural similarities are found between adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ALDP) and ABCD2 or ABCD3 and ABCD4.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 legend based on structural comparison.

claim: The model of ABCD2 and ABCD3 is predicted by Alphafold.
source: The model of ABCD2 and ABCD3 is predicted by Alphafold.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 legend.
